About

Psychology-focused student interested in mental health, human behavior, and access to care. I founded a youth-led peer-support initiative, research harm-reduction policy with a Johns Hopkins biostatistician, and connect writing and music to service, a consistent through-line of using evidence and empathy to support young people.

Leonia High School, Leonia, NJ · Expected June 2027
GPA 4.7 weighted / 3.84 unweighted · 10 AP courses (5 completed, 5 senior year) incl. AP Psychology · National, Rho Kappa & Science Honor Societies

AP Scholar with Distinction (College Board, 2026).

Certifications, Psychological First Aid (PFA) and Skills for Psychological Recovery (SPR), completed through the NCTSN / National Center for PTSD (2026).

Research

Independent Public Health Policy Research2024 to Present
  • Conduct harm-reduction policy research alongside a Johns Hopkins biostatistician, applying spatial and quantitative analysis to questions of public health and human behavior.
  • Analyze block-level spatial data on NYC supervised consumption sites to identify neighborhood-level patterns in public drug use.
  • Connect findings to active policy debates on supervised consumption, linking quantitative evidence to real public health decisions.
  • Authored the resulting paper, “Beyond the Facility Walls: A Geospatial Analysis on Supervised Consumption Sites and Its Neighborhood Effects,” which was accepted for publication by the National High School Journal of Science (NHSJS) in 2026 after peer review and revision.
Research poster, “Beyond the Facility Walls: A Geospatial Analysis of Supervised Consumption Sites and Neighborhood Effects,” co-presented with Eunice Cho.

Mental Health & Youth Advocacy

VOY Mental Health Initiative, Founder & President2024 to Present
  • Founded a student-led mental health initiative after identifying gaps in peer support, growing it into an ongoing program of wellness and stress-management resources.
  • Designed and launched Mo Soop (April 2026), an anonymous peer-support app where students share stress without judgment and find encouragement, modeled on the Korean idea of a safe “bamboo forest.”
  • Led a Finals Relief Project: student volunteers 3D-printed and donated 150 stress-relief clickers to Fort Lee High School during finals season.
  • Conceived and launched Mo Ri (October 2026), an app that helps high school students with ADHD handle both school and social situations. While developing Mo Ri, read research on ERIC and reports from the CDC and CHADD, and completed CHADD’s ADHD 101 course.
Open Mo Soop Open Mo Ri
“Benched”: College Athlete Mental Health Documentary, Co-Creator & Mental Health Lead2025 to Present
  • Co-creating a short documentary on how NCAA athletes navigate identity, mental health, and the pull between athletic demands and life after sports.
  • Lead the film’s psychological framing and athlete outreach, shaping interviews and linking subjects to peer mental health resources.
  • Developing a companion policy brief on supporting student-athlete wellbeing, with plans to submit the film to student festivals.
Mia’s Feelings Lab: Psychology Chapter-Book Series (Ages 7 to 10), Author2026 to Present
  • Wrote four books in the series, illustrated by Sharon Kwon, and self-published them on Amazon in 2026. Each book answers an emotional question kids ask: why they get angry, feel shy around new people, feel left out, or feel scared of the dark.
  • Grounds each story in real psychology, from the amygdala’s alarm system to social pain and cognitive distortions, and closes every book with a hands-on “Feelings Lab” activity that helps children apply the idea to their own lives.
  • An exercise in translating clinical concepts into warm, age-appropriate storytelling.
Why Do I Get So Angry?View on AmazonWhy Am I Shy Around New People?View on AmazonWhy Do I Feel Left Out?View on AmazonWhy Am I Scared of the Dark?View on Amazon
New Sky Auto Body, Wellness Program Intern2026
  • Invited by the shop’s owner to help ease strain among the younger technicians, designing and facilitating workplace sessions on communication, stress management, and coping with personal hardship.
  • The sessions surfaced long-standing misunderstandings among the staff and helped resolve them; the owner credited the program with noticeably improved workplace relationships.
  • A rare chance to apply psychology outside the classroom, with adults, in a real workplace.

Leadership & Community Service

Bergen County Youth Assembly (BCYA), Founder & Chair2025 to Present
  • Founded a nonpartisan, student-led youth organization serving Bergen County; active since November 2025 and formally established on July 11, 2026.
  • Serves as Director of Youth Mental Wellness, leading the group’s mental-wellness work alongside free student resources and peer tutoring delivered through schools and community partners.
  • Wrote and edited The Reset, a stress and resilience toolkit for high school students (a guide, a wallet card, and a stress-relief clicker) with a companion one-page guide for parents and trusted adults. A Bergen Community College psychology professor reviewed it before release; distribution is in preparation.
  • Led distribution of 300 printed copies of Before You Vote, a student-written BCYA guide to elections and first-time voting, to Bergen County public libraries and a high school.
